text: Every camp keeps four Kin: an **Elder**, a **Drummer**, a **Hunter** and a **Weaver**. They wander within **16 blocks** of their camp and never despawn. Right-click any of them to see their job and your rank with the tribe.

pages.title: The Elder
text: The Elder trades once you are a **Guest**. Each tribe has six offers, two for each rank from Guest to Kin, and every trade earns **+2** standing.

pages.title: Trading with the Elder
text: An Elder has nothing for a Stranger. Bring an offering to the hearth first.

Stock is limited. An offer can be taken **12 times** a day, **8** if it asks for two different items, and **6** if it sells a creature reagent. The Elder restocks once every Minecraft day, and closing the screen does not refill it.
When you reach **Voice**, talk to the Elder once more. They press the tribe's **Tribe Mark** into your hand, once for each tribe. Keep it safe: it becomes a [Kinship Totem](kinship_totem).

pages.title: The Drummer
text: Every **6 seconds** the Drummer strikes a beat that feeds **2 Pulse** into each Drumheart, Ley Collector and Pulse Resonator within **8 blocks**. Wind Harps, Wave Drums and Ember Horns take none of it. The beat also keeps nearby totems awake.

pages.title: The Hunter
text: The Hunter watches the camp's edge and strikes hostile mobs within **12 blocks**. Hurt any Kin, though, and the Hunter comes for you for a **minute**.

pages.title: The Weaver
text: Every **40 to 90 seconds** the Weaver walks to the nearest loom within **12 blocks** of camp (or a Song Bench, if there is no loom) and works it for **six seconds**. That pose is the work. It does not craft anything for you.

pages.title: Living beside them
text: Kin are neutral and patient. They will stand beside your machines, drum for your generators and guard your nights for as long as you like.
Never hit them. A stray sword swing costs **25** standing and turns the whole camp against you. See [Tribes and standing](standing) for everything else that angers a tribe.
The four spawn eggs are for creative builders who want to set up a camp of their own.
